etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: それ (sore, “that”) + なら (nara, “if”), literally "if that".

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Reduplication of まあ (interjection).
Resemblance to Cantonese 麻麻地 (maa4 maa4-2 dei6-2) (“so-so”) likely coincidental.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Borrowed from English cooler.
First cited to 1959.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from 信ずる (shinzuru). Natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Classical Japanese verb 冷(さ)む (samu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 冷む entry.
Related to 寒(さむ)い (samui, “cold (weather)”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/opo/ → /ofo/ → /owo/ → /oː/
From Old Japanese 大 (opo), from Proto-Japonic *əpə.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 愛 (MC 'ojH).
Compare modern Mandarin 愛／爱 (ài).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Originally a compound of 真 (ma, “true, genuine”) + な (na), an Old Japanese version of modern Japanese の (no, possessive particle).
The use of 愛 here is an example of ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Used as nanori in various names. 愛 is a very common element in many names.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 決(き)まる (kimaru, “to be decided, to be concluded”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 治む (wosamu). Attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE, and the Man'yōshū of circa 759 CE. Ultimately from Proto-Japonic *wosamu (“to control”). Cognate with 収(おさ)める (osameru).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 治む entry.
Likely derived ultimately from 長(おさ) (osa, “boss, chief, controller, ruler”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kwa/ → /ka/
From Middle Chinese 渦 (MC kwa, “eddy, swirl, whirlpool”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese verb 訪ぬ (tadunu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
